source.title: Reverse replay of behavioural sequences in hippocampal place cells during the awake state.

confidence_rationale: The named substrate anchor for MECH-319. Foster & Wilson establish that hippocampal place-cell sequences replay during awake immobility in a temporally REVERSED order immediately after experience -- demonstrating that the brain has a discriminable, internally-generated replay signature distinct from real behaviour. This grounds the SUBSTRATE-AVAILABILITY premise of MECH-319 (a categorical, tag-able simulation/replay event exists). It does NOT test the REE-novel write-gating function, so confidence is set for the substrate premise only, not the gate.
failure_signatures: The paper demonstrates that replay EXISTS and is discriminable, but it explicitly proposes replay as a mechanism FOR learning (reinforcement-style evaluation of event sequences) -- i.e. replay drives plasticity. MECH-319's gate must therefore SUPPRESS updates only for non-realized (ghost/DMN) passes while permitting real-experience replay to teach; a blanket simulation-mode write-block that caught all replay would contradict the learning role shown here.
Nothing in the recording addresses whether arbitration-weight (or any synaptic) updates are categorically gated by a simulation tag; the write-gate is entirely unobserved here.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Hippocampal place cells replay recent spatial experience during awake rest immediately after the experience, in a temporally REVERSED order; this awake reverse replay is suggestive of a role in the evaluation of event sequences in the manner of reinforcement-learning models and may be a general mechanism of learning and memory.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-319 presumes the substrate hosts discriminable simulation/replay passes that a categorical write-gate could key on. Foster & Wilson supply the foundational evidence that internally-generated, temporally-structured replay events exist and are distinguishable from on-line behaviour -- the existence-of-a-tag-able-replay-mode premise on which MECH-319's gate (and MECH-094's hypothesis-tag principle) depends.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This establishes ONLY that replay exists and is discriminable; it provides no evidence for a write-suppression gate keyed to a simulation tag, and it actually frames replay as a vehicle FOR learning -- so it supports the substrate premise while being neutral-to-tension on the gating function itself.
mapping.source_context: Rats; tetrode ensemble recording of CA1 place cells on a linear track, replay measured during awake immobility after running.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational Nature paper, gold-standard ensemble electrophysiology -- top source quality. Mapping fidelity moderate because it supports only the substrate-availability half of MECH-319 (replay exists / is discriminable), not the write-gate. Transfer risk standard rodent-hippocampus -> REE-arbitration-layer.
